findings.title: Count severity/header occurrences instead of matching physical lines
findings.detail: The new parser counts lines containing ERROR:/FATAL: and fullmatches the selected line with an unrestricted message tail. Two verbose headers on one line therefore count as one; a second malformed severity line without colon is excluded. Both actual-function probes retain42501 and single_header=True, despite the mandatory Root e4d829 rule requiring null for malformed/multiple headers.

required_contract.rule: Only one exact ERROR/FATAL header with a fixed13 state exports the state. Unknown/malformed/multiple headers export null and a fixed redaction class.

findings.impact: Retained unexpected-failure attribution can incorrectly claim one known SQLSTATE/source-confirmed diagnostic from malformed or multiple severity/header input. This matters to the bounded correction purpose of trustworthy partial evidence.
findings.limits: No permission escalation, SQL change, binder-verdict bypass or actual historical database cause is demonstrated. Existing exact binder predicate and positive commit/result checks remain independent.
findings.bounded_correction: Change only the new header classifier and focused regressions in a separately preserved replacement freeze. Detect all severity/header candidates, including inline second verbose headers and malformed severity lines, require exactly one valid header, and return null/fixed redaction on ambiguity. Keep fixed13 set, closed source metadata/frame/body/line projection, source before/after hashing, operation verdict, Session/finalizer/global-zero/persistent-IO paths and cleanup unchanged. Do not edit this freeze.
